one_sentence_story: George Miller proved in 1956 that immediate memory isn't limited by raw data size, only by holding roughly five to nine 'chunks' — so bundling scattered details into meaningful groups multiplies what your mind can grasp.
so_what_for_you: Stop trying to hold ten loose facts in your head at once; group phone digits, study notes, and project tasks into three or four labeled buckets.
